analysis:
Both files are CI-only (.github/actions/provider-ci-build/action.yml, .github/workflows/ci.yml). They touch no provider runtime code, coordinator protocol, keys, attestation, App Attest authorization or prefix-cache storage. T-041 was supplied as context but is not affected, because it covers the provider's runtime prefix cache, not CI caches. No T-0xx/TB-0xx security control is weakened.

Changed behavior examined:
1. Cache writes are now gated. SAVE_CACHES is true only for push events on master or dev (ci.yml lines 17-25). The composite action takes a save-caches input that defaults to 'false' (action.yml lines 7-9, 107, 116, 143). Pull requests previously saved caches scoped to their merge ref; they now save none. This narrows cache-poisoning surface by untrusted PR code, and the mimo-audio and cluster save steps are gated the same way.
2. A SwiftPM repositories cache is added (action.yml lines 47-53, 115-120). It is restored on PRs but saved only from trusted pushes. Its key is bound to OS, home layout, lane and the Package.resolved hash. It restores bare dependency clones, and SwiftPM resolves by pinned revision, so content-addressed commits limit tampering. Restore-key prefix fallback only widens reuse within the trusted-save set.
3. A .git cache is added to every checkout in ci.yml. It is restored, then actions/checkout runs over it with persist-credentials: false. If that checkout fails, the workspace is deleted and a cold checkout runs. The save step runs immediately after checkout and before any PR code executes, so saved .git cannot carry PR-built artifacts. Auth is removed from .git/config when persist-credentials is false, which keeps the job token out of the cache. Full-history Docs Lint uses a separate git-full-v1 key family. Saves happen only on master/dev pushes, so PR jobs only consume base-branch caches.
4. Sparse checkout excludes docs/reports/**/*.gz and landing/public/**/*.mp4. These are presumably read only by Docs Lint, which does a full checkout; that is a performance change and I saw no security gate affected.
5. The cluster cache key now strips git-describe text from submodule status (awk '{print $1,$2}'). Submodule SHAs are still bound into the key.

Remaining unverified: steps after checkout (the release-integrity gates, for example) are not visible beyond the patch. If any step reads refs such as origin/master or tags that a stale restored .git could hold, it could see outdated data. I saw no evidence of this. No finding is raised because the change is CI-only and the trust model for trusted-push saves is sound.
